clue.text: Pipe band's leader chasing sailors, wearing Chanel

indicators.note: the band's leader comes after, as if chasing, the rest
the designer's name is put on like clothing, so it goes round the sailors

parts.note: Coco Chanel, the French fashion designer
RN is the Royal Navy

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A pipe band's leader runs after some sailors while dressed in Chanel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pipe' looks like part of the pipe band but stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A corncob pipe is a tobacco pipe whose bowl is made from a hollowed maize cob.

clue.text: Lord Copper edging closer to junior doctors

definitions.note: used as an exclamation of surprise, like 'Gosh!'

indicators.note: copper's letters form an edge around the next piece

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: the closer of a word is its final letter

parts.note: MBs are Bachelors of Medicine, i.e. doctors

explanation.surface: Lord Copper, the press baron from Waugh's Scoop, sidles up to some junior doctors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lord Copper' reads as one name, but 'Lord' is the definition as an exclamation and 'Copper' the element.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild British exclamations of surprise, interchangeable as in 'Crikey!'

clue.text: Standing on couch with foot in bandage

parts.note: re means on or concerning
to couch something is to put it into words

indicators.note: in a down clue the foot of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone stands with a bandaged foot resting on a couch.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing as reputation or status: a person's good name in the community.

clue.text: Result of flying high over River Wye, reportedly in reverse direction

indicators.note: the vapour trail is spread over, covering, the river letter

parts.note: a vapour trail left by a high-flying aircraft

indicators.note: signals that the river's name is to be taken as heard

parts.note: the River Wye on the Welsh border; its name is said like the letter Y

explanation.surface: A plane leaves a trail high over the River Wye, going the other way, so we're told.
explanation.definitionFit: Contrarily means in the opposite way or direction, contrary to the expected course.

clue.text: Barnet lad discontented copper

parts.note: Barnet is Cockney rhyming slang for hair (Barnet Fair), and a bob is a haircut

indicators.note: the content, the middle letter, is removed

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A boy from Barnet in north London is an unhappy policeman.
explanation.walkthrough: Barnet is a London borough, but here it is rhyming slang for hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Bobby is British slang for a policeman, after Sir Robert Peel; copper is another slang term.

clue.text: Rotate teepee

parts.note: tee is the spelt-out name of the letter T
widdle is a childish word for urinating

explanation.surface: An instruction to spin a wigwam round.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the single word into two halves: 'tee' gives its letter and 'pee' a nursery synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: To twiddle a knob or dial is to turn it round idly with the fingers.

clue.text: Land or borough in Holland for Spooner

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the opening sounds of word pairs

parts.note: something from Holland is Dutch
a borough is a town

explanation.surface: Seems to ask for a word meaning land or a Dutch borough.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of DUTCH TOWN gives TOUCH DOWN.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft's touchdown is the moment it lands on the runway.

clue.text: Regularly nibble and kiss horny mountaineer

indicators.note: take every second letter of the following word

parts.note: X is a written kiss

explanation.surface: A frisky climber nibbles and kisses at regular intervals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horny' suggests lust but means having horns.
explanation.definitionFit: The ibex is a wild goat with great curved horns that lives on steep mountain crags.

clue.text: Starts to denounce inequality and social division in rant

indicators.note: the first letter of each of the next three words

parts.note: a tribe is a social group or division

explanation.surface: A speech denouncing inequality and class division turns into a rant.
explanation.definitionFit: A diatribe is a bitter, forceful verbal attack, much like a rant.

clue.text: In row D?

parts.note: D is the letter at the end of the word end, so it is that word's end; and placed in a line

explanation.surface: Asks whether a theatre seat is in row D.
explanation.definitionFit: Arranged end to end means placed in a line, one after another, as in a row.

clue.text: Nancy's one swan is set free

parts.note: Nancy is a French city, and un is French for one
a pen is a female swan

explanation.surface: Nancy's only swan has been released.
explanation.walkthrough: Nancy looks like a woman's name but is the city in north-east France.
explanation.definitionFit: To unpen an animal is to let it out of its enclosure, liberating it.

clue.text: Bouncy, half-cut barman turns and departs for walk

indicators.note: only the first half of the word is kept
the composer's name is read backwards

parts.note: a whimsical name for a composer, a man who writes bars of music: Ravel
D is the timetable abbreviation for departs

explanation.surface: A lively, tipsy barman spins round and leaves for a stroll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-cut' suggests drunk, but it halves the word before it; 'barman' is not a bartender.
explanation.definitionFit: A boulevard is a broad tree-lined avenue, often a promenade for walking along.

clue.text: Gamble with a contraceptive method? A brainwave!

parts.note: to bet is to gamble
the rhythm method avoids conception by timing

explanation.surface: Someone suddenly decides to trust to the rhythm method and calls it inspired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A brainwave!' sounds like a bright idea but is literal: an electrical wave in the brain.
explanation.definitionFit: Beta rhythm is a pattern of electrical activity in the alert brain, one type of brainwave.

clue.text: Every so often go crazy over pasta

indicators.note: take every second letter of the words

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Now and then someone goes mad over pasta.
explanation.definitionFit: Orzo is small rice-shaped pasta, an Italian type used in soups.

clue.text: Group including copper and bishop run down hill backwards

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: the two words are read in reverse

parts.note: to slate is to criticise harshly
a mesa is a flat-topped hill

explanation.surface: A group of coppers and a bishop roll back down a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests police; here it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Base metals are the non-precious ones, a class including copper, lead and zinc.

clue.text: Cairo-born criminal ringing commercial dating agency

indicators.note: the scrambled letters form a ring round the advert
a criminal arrangement of letters means they are scrambled

parts.note: an ad is a commercial

explanation.surface: An Egyptian-born crook phones an advert for a dating agency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dating agency' means not matchmaking but what fixes the age of objects.
explanation.definitionFit: Carbon-14 decay lets scientists estimate the age of organic remains, so it is an agent of dating.

clue.text: Dry-eyed husband angrily stifling curses

indicators.note: the rearranged letters smother the curse inside them
the letters are thrown about in temper

parts.note: drat is a mild curse

explanation.surface: A dry-eyed husband fumes, holding back his swearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dry-eyed' reads as one word but splits: 'Dry' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To dehydrate something is to remove the water from it, i.e. to make it dry.

clue.text: Obscure boozer between centre of Cleveleys and Morecambe?

indicators.note: the middle letter of the nine-letter town name

parts.note: a sot is a drunkard
Eric Morecambe, the British comedian

explanation.surface: A pub somewhere between two Lancashire seaside towns, Cleveleys and Morecambe, is little known.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boozer' suggests a British pub but is a drinker; Morecambe is a resort but here the comic.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric means understood only by a few, hence obscure.

clue.text: Nipper picked up poems and scanned lines

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting the word up reads it from bottom to top

parts.note: a crab nips with its pincers, so it is a nipper
odes are lyric poems

explanation.surface: A child picks up some poems and scans their lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nipper' suggests a child, and 'scanned lines' suggests verse metre; both mislead.
explanation.definitionFit: Barcodes are rows of printed stripes read by a laser scanner at a shop till.

clue.text: Coppers slam heartless order to leave train

indicators.note: the inner letters of the word are removed

parts.note: 'All change!' is the British call telling passengers to get off at the end of the line

explanation.surface: Police slam a cruel order for passengers to leave a train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' suggests police but means copper coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Coppers are low-value coins, the loose coins one carries.

clue.text: Crude paddles in dugout canoe

indicators.note: the paddles go inside the hollowed word
the word is dug out, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: oars are paddles

explanation.surface: Rough paddles lie in a dugout canoe.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse and crude both mean rough, unrefined or vulgar.

clue.text: Test a Tesla stock car

indicators.note: the phrase holds the answer in stock, among its letters

explanation.surface: Try a Tesla stock car on the track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stock car' reads as one phrase but 'stock' is the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate is a British car with a long body and rear door, a station wagon.

clue.text: One ignored unspoken diplomacy

indicators.note: something ignored is left out of account, so the numeral is dropped from the word for unspoken

parts.note: tacit means understood without being stated
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Diplomacy where one person is quietly snubbed.
explanation.definitionFit: Tact is sensitivity in dealing with others, the essence of diplomacy.

clue.text: Cheating outrageously at ludo, Sue is probed by copper at last

indicators.note: the anagram has the next piece pushed into it
the letters behave wildly and are rearranged
take the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Sue cheats outrageously at ludo and a policeman finally investigates.
explanation.definitionFit: Adulterous describes cheating on a spouse, being unfaithful.

clue.text: Club finally lost extremely tight game

indicators.note: that letter is taken away

parts.note: tight means drunk, and blotto means very drunk

indicators.note: take the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A club side has lost a very close match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely tight' looks like a close game but means very drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotto is a lottery or a bingo-style game of chance.

clue.text: Opposed to social worker removing kids from Sid

parts.note: an ant is a worker in a social insect colony

indicators.note: those letters are taken out of the name

parts.note: kids as sons and daughters, S and D

explanation.surface: Someone objects to a social worker taking Sid's children into care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Social worker' is the insect, not the profession.
explanation.definitionFit: Anti as a preposition means against or opposed to.

clue.text: Twisted and turned more than needed

indicators.note: the letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: Something has been twisted and turned beyond what was required.
explanation.definitionFit: Redundant means superfluous, surplus to requirements.

clue.text: Either end of ancient American vessel

parts.note: the end of the word ancient is A or T, written out as A-OR-T

explanation.surface: Either end of an old American ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Spell out the choice literally: either end is 'A or T'.
explanation.definitionFit: The body's main artery is a blood vessel, carrying blood from the heart.

clue.text: Struggling to evacuate county town of Cornwall, briefly

indicators.note: the last letter is cut off

parts.note: St Ives is a seaside town in Cornwall, England's south-western tip

explanation.surface: An attempt to evacuate a Cornish town runs into trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Evacuate' suggests clearing a town of people but means emptying the bowels.
explanation.definitionFit: Costive means constipated, having difficulty passing stools.

clue.text: Having lost perp stupidly, poor copper's been blue

indicators.note: letters of the criminal are taken out of the pool
the removed letters may come out in any jumbled order
the remaining letters are poorly arranged and must be rearranged

parts.note: perp is slang for the perpetrator of a crime

explanation.surface: A useless policeman, having foolishly let the culprit go, is depressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue' suggests sad but means smutty.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue jokes or films are indecent or smutty, i.e. obscene.
